title: Thoracic 3-vertebra segments (T2-T4, T7-T9): moments and relative rotations at failure in dynamic sagittal bending (2 rad/s), pediatric vs adult

quantity.name: failure moment and relative rotation
quantity.definition: moments measured at the inferior and superior ends (load cells at the supports) and relative angles of the extreme vertebrae to the central one (Vicon, CT-registered local systems) at the instant of tissue failure

source.authors: Lopez-Valdes FJ, Lau S, Riley P, Lamp J, Kent R
source.sample: 8 thoracic 3-vertebra segments (T2-T4 and T7-T9) from 4 PMHS: F470 female 7 y 119 cm 27 kg; M485 male 15 y 163 cm 50 kg; M319 male 52 y 179 cm 77 kg; M320 male 48 y 168 cm 68 kg; all ligaments except intertransverse preserved; 37.1 C saline bath

protocol.summary: Servohydraulic machine driving a linkage that rotates both potted end vertebrae in the sagittal plane (cups free to translate horizontally); preconditioning (1 Hz), 5 non-injurious dynamic ramp-and-hold tests D1-D5, then failure ramp at nominal 2 rad/s (failure amplitude 11.7-20.6 deg per specimen, Table 2).
how_to_simulate: Model the 3-vertebra thoracic segment with discs and all ligaments except intertransverse; pot the two end vertebrae
Impose equal and opposite sagittal rotations of the end vertebrae at ~2 rad/s (frontal-impact type bending) with the end supports free to translate horizontally
Record moments at both ends and joint relative rotations; compare failure moment and angle per specimen (adult vs pediatric), injury pattern (IS/SS tear, facet dislocation) qualitatively
protocol.notes: Single specimens (n=1 per row), no means. Injuries (Table 4): mostly IS and SS complete tear with facet dislocation; T7-T9 adults also disc rupture/vertebral body fracture. Preconditioning and ramp-and-hold moment curves (Figs 4-7) not digitised.
